claude_analysis.pricing_assessment: The extracted $1-$8 'prices' come from the frontiersin.org HAPPE paper, which describes a free academic pipeline, so they are probably text artifacts rather than real prices; commercial tools like encevis PureEEG and Clean EEG point to lab-license pricing of roughly $1000/yr (an assumption, since no real price was observed), under pressure from free tools like EEGLAB, HAPPE and MNE.
claude_analysis.legal_reasoning: The regulatory probe found no restriction signals (0 restriction hits, 0 government sources) for research-use software, but clinical diagnostic use would probably need medical-device clearance, which was not checked.
